Subject: MSA + Order Form: confirm content-use carveouts and productization handoff

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks again for the redlines — I attached a marked-up MSA with inline comments to make next steps concrete (Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). A few specific asks from our side to help the legal and procurement teams converge quickly: 

- Can you confirm whether CobaltTech requires an affirmative assignment of output title (i.e., a clause saying customer owns "Customer Content Derived Outputs") or whether a non-exclusive output license with productization carveouts is acceptable?
- For training: do you require a blanket opt-out of any model improvement (training), or would a scoped opt-out limited to customer-owned data plus an audit/evidence path work?
- For feedback: your redline proposes a wide feedback license for Redwood to use customer feedback "for any purpose" — please confirm whether a narrower feedback license (product improvement only, non-sublicensable) would be acceptable.

To speed ops validation, Ben and Karthik are looped in to outline operational controls (audit logs, telemetry retention, private deployment options) and an evidence checklist we can attach to the order form if needed.

If you can respond with the preferred option on output title + training by EOD Thursday (12 Jul), we will produce two alternate snippets (Assignment vs. License + carveouts) and a short MAP for procurement.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx (docx)

Best,

Lauren Bishop

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: confirm content-use carveouts and productization handoff

Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed with procurement and our outside counsel and have a few high level positions: 

1) Output ownership: CobaltTech prefers title to outputs where the output is a direct derivation of Customer Content (e.g., templates, scraped rows that are verbatim customer inputs). For ephemeral/generated content that is not a direct "copy" of customer input, we're open to a narrow non-exclusive license with downstream restrictions (no resale of models trained on our data).

2) Training: Our default is to opt out of any training. That said, we are open to a controlled opt-in for aggregated/anonymized telemetry where Redwood can demonstrate robust de-identification + an audit trail. We will provide a proposed definition of "de-identified" and a short list of telemetry types we consider non-customer content.

3) Feedback license: we cannot accept an unlimited grant. Proposed: Redwood can use feedback solely for product improvements and must not sublicense or republish customer confidential content.

I've attached the redline we returned to our counsel (CobaltTech_Requested_Changes.pdf). Mayur from procurement is on copy — he'll coordinate the MAP timeline.

On timing — we need proposed alternative language by Friday 13 Jul COB.

Best,

Elena Ruiz
Head of GAI Program
CobaltTech
elena.ruiz@cobalttech.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobalttech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed language options + operational notes (output / training / feedback)

Elena / team — attaching two compact language options below to simplify negotiation. Both are intentionally short so legal can drop them straight into the order form. Please consider Option A (Assignment) vs Option B (Limited License + carveouts).

Option A — Assignment (customer-owned outputs where outputs are direct reproductions):
"Customer Content Derivatives. Redwood hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in Customer Content Derivatives that are established to be direct reproductions or narrowing extracts of Customer Content; for all other Generated Content Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use such Generated Content for Customer's internal business purposes; Redwood retains rights to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for model improvement."

Option B — Limited Output License + Productization Carveout:
"Generated Content License. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Generated Content arising from Customer Content for Customer's internal business purposes. Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Generated Content to produce models intended for resale to third parties when such models are materially derived from Customer Content; Redwood may use anonymized and aggregated telemetry for product improvement subject to the de-identification standard in Exhibit A."

Feedback license (both options — narrower text):
"Feedback. Customer may provide feedback. Redwood may use Feedback only to improve Redwood's services and products and shall not sublicense or publish Customer Confidential Information contained in Feedback."

Operational notes (brief):
- Private deployments / Dedicated capacity: when customers require stronger custody controls (no telemetry export), we can enable Dedicated mode and short-circuit telemetry export.
- Evidence path: we can include an "evidence exhibit" listing log retention windows, sample audit entries, and a sign-off workflow for de-identification checks.

If either option is acceptable, we'll generate redline-ready text and the MAP for procurement. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Regards,

Ben Carter
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Ops feasibility + evidence checklist (attached)

Quick operational follow-up: attached is a short training evidence checklist we use for customers who accept scoped training (training_evidence_checklist.xlsx). Highlights:

- De-identification standard: candidate fields we remove/mask, and a minimum 90-day hold period before telemetry is eligible for aggregate training.
- Audit artifacts: examples of KV cache logs, request ids, and the sample format we can include in Exhibit A.
- Dedicated option: if CobaltTech selects Dedicated capacity or Private deployment, telemetry export can be disabled and we can provide a signed attestation for data flows.

Practical ask: if you go with Option B + de-identification, we need a short sample dataset (redacted) and one compliance contact to run a single audit snapshot prior to signing. That snapshot is low friction and can be scheduled during procurement onboarding.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer

- CobaltTech: legal will review the Option B redline and return comments by Tue 17 Jul.
